svg.text: Bilge Pumps & CO Detection — the Two Systems That Save Lives Unattended
Float switch — parallel wiring
Either one energized runs the pump —
wired in parallel, not series.
Pump runs even with panel switch OFF
Sizing: 1,500-3,500 GPH typical coastal.
Manual backup pump required per USCG on Class 2+.
Carbon monoxide detection
Odorless, colorless — incapacitates at
200 ppm, lethal rapidly above 1,600 ppm.
Mount at BREATHING height, not ceiling
CO disperses through the cabin, unlike
propane (sinks) or smoke (rises).
Required in every sleeping space + adjacent to enclosed engine/genset spaces.
The 4-minute blower rule — USCG 33 CFR 175.110
Gasoline-powered vessels must run the bilge blower for 4 minutes before starting the engine —
clearing accumulated fuel vapor from the engine space before the ignition source arrives.
No shortcut here — this rule exists because gasoline vapor explosions in engine compartments are real and fast.
Wiring for the worst day, not the average day
A dedicated "auto" circuit selection with both manual and auto options is the cleaner, safer install
pattern versus a bare parallel tap — but the underlying logic is the same: the pump must run when the
boat needs it, regardless of what position the operator left the switch in.
